label: “Reduce charge while keeping cell permeability.”
prompt: Reduce charge while keeping cell permeability. (peptide design)
answerHead:
BioMate

Cyclic Peptide Design — Reduces net charge on peptide scaffolds while predicting cell permeability, binding affinity, serum stability, and aggregation risk against a target protein structure.

Input: BCL-XL structure (1BXL.pdb) as receptor; BAK BH3 reference sequence (GQVGRQLAIIGDDINR) as the peptide scaffold; charge-reduction mode enabled; cyclization chemistry specified
Key steps:
Enumerate charge-reducing substitutions (acidic Asp/Glu → polar Asn/Gln; basic Lys/Arg → polar Ser/Thr) while preserving the BH3 binding motif
Score each variant for predicted binding ΔG (docking/FoldX), membrane permeability (logD, TPSA, H-bond count), and serum stability (proteolytic cleavage risk)
Rank candidates by multi-objective trade-off: net charge reduction vs. affinity retention vs. permeability gain
Expected output: Ranked peptide sequences (FASTA) with per-variant predictions: net charge, predicted binding affinity (kcal/mol ± SEM), permeability score, aggregation propensity, solubility estimate; docking poses (PDB); design rationale JSON

Important: This workflow does not read your attached peptide_candidates.fasta or peptide_constraints.json — it generates and scores variants parametrically. If you want to screen your pre-enumerated candidate set against BCL-XL and rank them by permeability + charge, I can find a peptide-binding prediction workflow that accepts FASTA input directly. Which would you prefer — let this workflow generate new charge-optimized variants, or score your existing candidates?
